To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the xanthophyl cycle is a pH-regulated process, that the pH-regulation is achieved through the pH-dependent activation of violaxanthin deep oxidase and that this activation is achieved by the pH-dependent conformational change of the enzyme.
The structure of violaxanthin deep oxidase (VDE) reveals a lipocalin dimer that opens up to bind its two violaxanthins at low pH.

(1) VDEcd is a monomer at neutral pH and a dimer at low pH, and (2) the pH-dependent dimerization of VDEcd opens a channel in the protein that allows the deepoxidation of both β-ionone rings of the substrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of the pH-dependent xanthophyll conversion and the regulation of the VDE activity in vivo.
the structure, function, regulation and evolution of the enzymes of the violaxanthin cycle.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the xanthophyl cycle and its regulation by pH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pH-induced structural change is the molecular basis of the pH-dependent activity of VDE.
the VDEcd structures at acidic pH are consistent with the proposed mechanism of the xanthophyl cycle.
the xanthophyllic cycle in plants is a very complex mechanism, which has been studied for many years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the xanthophyllic cycle in plants is an adaptation to the changing light conditions.
VDEcd has a pH-dependent conformational switch that controls its activity and membrane attachment.
we have shown that the VDEcd dimer structure is the functional form of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH-dependent regulation of VDE is based on a pH-dependent conformational change that opens up the lipocalin barrel to allow substrate access and the binding of two violaxanthins at the same time.
the pH-dependent xanthophyll deepoxidase activity is the result of a structural rearrangement of the lipocalin barrel, which is induced by the protonation of a histidine residue.
VDEcd is a monomeric, inactive lipocalin at neutral pH that is converted into a dimeric, active lipocalin upon acidification.
